title: Investigation of emotional processing of images in patients with borderline personality disorder compared to healthy controls
summary:
Many people with borderline personality disorder use self-injuring behavior (such as cutting) to relieve intense inner tension. While general negative triggers tend to cause more stress in these individuals than in healthy people, stimuli specifically related to self-injury can have a short-term calming effect on them. For instance, the sight of blood or the sensation of pain can reduce feelings of stress or tension in some patients. However, self-injurious behavior carries significant risks (e.g. infections, latent suicidality) and often becomes chronic because patients do not learn to regulate their emotions in alternative, functional ways.
To better understand how emotion regulation through self-injury works in patients with borderline personality disorder, research has lacked specifically suited image material. This study investigates the newly developed set of images "Emotional Picture Set of Self-Injury" (EPSI) that depict different phases and forms of self-injury. The goal is to determine how patients with borderline personality disorder react to these images compared to healthy individuals. During the presentation of the images, we will collect subjective measures (emotional rating and level of tension) and measure the participants' physical reactions (heart rate, sweating).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
General Inclusion Criteria:
- written informed consent for participation has been obtained

Patients:
- diagnosis of borderline personality disorder (BPD) based on DSM or ICD criteria
- a history of at least one documented episode of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI)
Exclusion criteria:
General Exclusion Criteria:
- pre-existing neurological or cardiovascular diseases, heart diseases

Patients:
- presence of acute suicidality
- presence of an acute depressive episode
- presence of the following comorbidities: psychotic disorders, mania, anxiety disorders, panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), current substance abuse

Controls:
- presence of any psychiatric disorder
